races.name: Michael Brunton Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Arctic Tsar
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's prominent-racing type has run twice on good ground already without winning or placing, but his natural racing position close to the pace is an asset in a race where Hackpen Hill sets an uncontested lead; Joe Leavy rides and 30 days since last run is unremarkable.

runners_data.name: Easy Answer
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's runner has placed once in two starts on good ground, but his instinct is to race from the rear — placed into midfield here because this field is unusually rich in hold-up types, which means Callum Shepherd may struggle to find the cover and late gap that suits this horse best.

runners_data.name: First Mate
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's horse has posted consecutive seventh-place finishes over 6f and 8f on good ground and is a natural hold-up runner; Tom Marquand will find this horse occupying a more forward map position than its true style demands, and its STYLE_FIT score of 0.90 tempers expectations accordingly — 8 days since its last run is a minor positive.

runners_data.name: Flick Of An Eye
runners_data.note: A completely unexposed debutant for Simon & Ed Crisford and David Probert with no form, going, or style data to anchor assessment; on fast ground over 6f at Salisbury, pure ability on debut could make the unknown profile either a danger or a non-factor.

runners_data.name: Gold Reef City
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's hold-up runner placed third on debut before dropping to seventh, giving a form string that suggests mild improvement is plausible; as a genuine closer, Gold Reef City needs Hackpen Hill's pace to be stronger than anticipated to generate the late real estate needed to close, 26 days off is routine.

runners_data.name: Goodwood Meteor
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's hold-up type has one run on good ground (sixth of six) and one on soft (ninth), meaning the step to good-to-firm here is an upgrade in conditions but his closing style remains dependent on a genuine gallop developing; 30 days since last run.

runners_data.name: Hackpen Hill
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter for Ed Walker and Kieran Shoemark, wearing headgear, with two runs on similar good ground showing consistent if unspectacular form; his primary advantage today is unchallenged control of the fractions from gate to line on this straight 6f track, 22 days since his last run suggesting freshness.

runners_data.name: Ongombo
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' hold-up horse has run twice on Standard (AW) ground, sixth and eighth, with no turf or good-ground experience; the move to Salisbury turf on good-to-firm is a significant surface question mark, and 44 days between runs is the longest freshen-up in the field, adding further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Saturn Star
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's second debutant in this race alongside Gold Reef City, ridden by Hector Crouch with no public form or style to evaluate; the Beckett yard's four winners from 39 runners over 14 days is a modest strike rate, so this runner must be assessed on trust in the operation rather than evidence.

runners_data.name: Forbidden Fire
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's debut runner is ridden by Oisin Murphy and carries 128lbs versus the field's 133lbs, representing the only weight advantage in the race — an intriguing flag for a trainer and jockey combination that regularly targets juvenile novices with well-prepared first-timers; style entirely unknown.

races.paceDynamic: Hackpen Hill is the confirmed sole front-runner and should stride into an uncontested lead from the gates, setting a sustainable tempo on good-to-firm ground over this 6f Salisbury straight track. With no other natural leader to push the pace, Hackpen Hill and Kieran Shoemark can dictate every fraction, controlling the gallop and denying rivals a target to chase down. The hold-up contingent — Gold Reef City, Goodwood Meteor, Ongombo, and Easy Answer — will be sprinting from further back into a compressed finish, a task made harder when the pace is moderate and the front-runner is allowed to coast. This race shape strongly favours prominent and front-running profiles: a lone, untroubled leader dictating on fast ground at Salisbury creates a bias toward those who can travel close to the pace from the outset, rather than those forced to make up ground late. Note that First Mate and Easy Answer are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because this field carries more off-pace types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Arctic Tsar and any unknown debutants with natural early pace are the runners most likely to press Hackpen Hill for the prominent positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hackpen Hill Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hackpen Hill sets a comfortable, uncontested lead and the field fails to close the gap in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Hackpen Hill dictates every fraction from the front, setting a pace that suits his stride on good-to-firm ground, and Shoemark can time any quickening perfectly without having to fight for position. Horses that travel prominently in his slipstream — including Arctic Tsar — are best placed to pounce if the leader tires, but a clean front-run on this track is historically hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutant Bursts Onto Scene
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed newcomers — Forbidden Fire, Flick Of An Eye, or Saturn Star — shows natural early pace or explosive late ability that negates the controlled tempo.
scenarios.body: Andrew Balding's Forbidden Fire (Oisin Murphy aboard) or Simon & Ed Crisford's Flick Of An Eye could arrive with unquantified ability that catches the field cold on debut, as is common in competitive 2yo novices on fast ground. The moderate, uncontested gallop set by Hackpen Hill actually suits a talented debutant who travels sweetly off the pace and has one sharp burst to deliver.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Hackpen Hill goes too fast for conditions or the good-to-firm ground rides quicker than expected, causing the front to collapse in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Gold Reef City or Goodwood Meteor, racing from their natural hold-up berths, would benefit from a strong pace that sets up a late run, closing through beaten horses in the final 100 yards. However, the probability is tempered significantly because Easy Answer and First Mate — the redistr­ibuted horses — are unlikely to fully replicate their natural closing style from a midfield map position, reducing the depth of the hold-up challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Midfield Battle
scenarios.trigger: If a contested early break creates a muddling, uneven gallop that fragments the field and produces an unpredictable result.
scenarios.body: If unexpected early crowding or a rival pressing Hackpen Hill disrupts the anticipated solo lead, the race devolves into a messy affair where positional chaos unsettles prominent types and hold-up runners alike. In this shape, a versatile, uncomplicated traveller who finds a clear run — potentially Saturn Star or Flick Of An Eye on debut — could emerge from the confusion.

watchPoints.text: Forbidden Fire carries 5lbs less than every other runner in the field — if Oisin Murphy deploys that weight advantage tactically on debut for Andrew Balding, watch for this horse to be produced at speed in the final 2f when rivals are tiring.

Hackpen Hill's headgear flag combined with two runs on good ground without troubling the judge raises the question of whether a lone front-run will see this horse find enough in the closing stages, or whether the lead simply flatters a horse that cannot quicken when challenged.

Easy Answer and First Mate are both natural hold-up horses mapped into midfield — if Callum Shepherd and Tom Marquand both attempt to slide back to their horses' preferred position early in the race, watch for a bunched, slow-starting rear group that leaves them with too much ground to make up.

The three debutants — Forbidden Fire, Flick Of An Eye, Saturn Star — collectively represent a major unknown block; if any one of them shows natural early speed and presses Hackpen Hill, the entire pace dynamic shifts from a solo lead to a contested gallop, dramatically altering the scenario probabilities.

Gold Reef City and Goodwood Meteor are genuine closers in a race likely to be run at a moderate, front-runner-friendly pace — watch their finishing positions as a guide to whether the good-to-firm ground is riding faster than declared and generating enough of a true gallop to bring them into play late.

races.name: Frazier Jones Wine Merchants Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: So Darn Hot
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Ed Walker and Kieran Shoemark, needs the pace to be genuinely contested to deliver a late run; recent form is uninspiring (0-6-7-0-5) and similar-going record of just one win from 15 runs is a concern — may find Dandana's controlled tempo too comfortable for rivals to crack open a gap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, So Darn Hot nonetheless rates top of these on our figures and has experience of today's distance and going. Fresh enough after 33 days, he carries 140 lb from stall one and looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Dr Strangelove
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes over for Oliver Cole on a horse that has placed consistently at 6-7f on good ground (2-2-3-4 in recent starts); sits naturally prominent and has strong claims if he can settle just off Dandana's shoulder without being shuffled wide by the prominent cluster.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and knocking hard on the door, Dr Strangelove has finished second twice and third once in his last three starts, and he has run over today's trip and going before — draw two, carrying 136 lb. The risk is that he remains winless in recent starts despite his solid profile.

runners_data.name: Dandana
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner for Simon & Ed Crisford, wearing a tongue-tie, fresh off a 16-day break with a win over this course and distance combination in the book; controls the race's tempo entirely and can choose the fractions — the key question is whether that advantage is enough to hold on in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment:
Dandana showed her best when winning one start back — sorry, a winner **five** starts back, and back in the mix with a fourth last time out after two unplaced efforts, she returns in good nick just 16 days on with experience over today's trip and going; the main risk is that she's been inconsistent in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Regional Rock
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old boasts a tidy record of 1W3P from four runs, all over 6f on good or soft ground, and Hector Crouch knows this track well; a natural prominent type who should find a comfortable berth in second or third and is the most consistent form horse in the field at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who has placed in three of his last four starts, with a win in the other, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the weight of 131 lb from stall 4 could prove the limiting factor against stronger-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: Golden Brown
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old has a win and place at 6f on similar ground but has been off 60 days, which is the longest layoff in the field; Rob Hornby keeps the ride and, on his best form, he handles prominent races well — fitness after the break is the one caveat.
runners_data.comment: Golden Brown won two starts back and was second the two runs before that, giving him a consistent placed profile over this trip and going; the main concern is that eight-week absence after that disappointing latest run.

runners_data.name: An Outlaw's Grace
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Richard Hannon and Sean Levey wearing a hood, with a plodding recent record (6-2-0-3-5-4) that masks three placed efforts at 6f on good ground; needs a stronger gallop than Dandana is likely to set, and the similar-going record of 0 wins from 15 runs flags a horse that often promises more than it delivers.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked last on our figures, An Outlaw's Grace faces a stiff ask at 128 lb from stall 3; a third three starts back is the best he can offer, though he has run over today's trip and going and returns on a reasonable 23-day break.

runners_data.name: Supreme King
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners a genuinely prominent-natured horse for David Evans that has been mapped to midfield purely because the field is saturated with early types; its true style fits races where it can be handy from the outset, and with that position likely compromised from the gate, its STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 signals a meaningful discount to its winning prospects here despite decent recent placed efforts.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in five of his last six starts — finishing seventh last time out after back-to-back seconds — Supreme King ranks sixth of seven on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and distance and a 14-day turnaround that suggests he's ready to run.

races.paceDynamic: Dandana is the confirmed lone front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, David Probert can dictate terms at a comfortable, controlled gallop on good to firm ground over six furlongs at Salisbury. The prominent brigade — Dr Strangelove, Regional Rock, Golden Brown, and Supreme King — will jostle for positions just off the pace, creating a competitive early order behind Dandana but not one that materially raises the tempo. With the pace sustainable rather than searching, horses racing prominently or tracking just off the leader will be ideally positioned for the home straight, giving the stalker/prominent profile the clearest route to victory. The field holds more prominent types than can all occupy their natural positions, and Regional Rock and Dr Strangelove — with their stronger in-race records — are most likely to actually secure the berths closest to Dandana.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dandana Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Dandana dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and prominent chasers run to form.
scenarios.body: Dandana sets a measured pace that suits those tracking within two lengths, leaving the hold-up horses with too much ground to make up in the closing furlong. Prominent racers who settle just behind the leader inherit the optimum position as the field fans out and the race is decided in the final 150 yards.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Dandana Stays On, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is sufficiently restrained that Dandana's stamina advantage over the prominent chasers proves decisive.
scenarios.body: Probert steals a lead that is never seriously threatened, and the prominent horses consume energy closing a gap they never quite bridge. Dandana's good-to-firm form (1/6f/GOO) and fresh enough prep (16 days) makes this outcome viable if rivals run into each other.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack press Dandana harder than expected, lifting the gallop and leaving the door ajar for the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated pace exhausts the early movers and allows So Darn Hot or An Outlaw's Grace to weave through late in the straight. This scenario requires genuine pressure on Dandana that the pace map suggests is unlikely given the redistribution of prominent types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Crowded Prominent Battle
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent types creates an early jostle that disrupts all their rhythms and opens the race up unpredictably.
scenarios.body: Supreme King, racing out of its natural berth due to field congestion, and the other prominent types expend extra energy establishing position, leaving the race in a muddled state through the first three furlongs. The resulting scramble could benefit any horse that finds daylight, but this scenario hinges on atypical chaos that the current setup makes unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Regional Rock and Dr Strangelove are both natural prominent types hunting the same berth directly behind Dandana — if they race wide or bump early, one or both will be compromised before halfway.

Supreme King's inability to secure its natural prominent position due to the crowded early order could see Oisin Murphy take a pull, placing a genuine pace horse further back than ideal and reducing its effectiveness.

Golden Brown's 60-day absence is the longest in the field — watch for any signs of rustiness in the market or under Hornby in the early strides, as a prominent horse that is less than fit can badly unbalance a tightly-grouped field.

Dandana's tongue-tie (hg:t) is worth monitoring at the start — if the filly is slow out of the stalls, the pace dynamic collapses entirely and the scenario probabilities shift sharply toward the prominent and hold-up horses.

Going reported consistently as Good to Firm across all Salisbury races today despite the card listing Good — fast ground benefits horses with high-cruising-speed prominent profiles and could sharpen Dandana's advantage if she gets the fractions exactly right.

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Stonehenge Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Dandyman Dan
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with recent form showing inconsistency (15943) and a step up to 1m first time; Oliver Cole yard in fair shape at T14:4/17 but this is unproven stamina territory, and he will face fierce early competition for the lead from at least three other speed-lovers.
runners_data.comment: Dandyman Dan arrives here fit on a 19-day turnaround, has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 104 marks him out as a live danger — third last time out shows he retains form. The risk is that he has been winless in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Firehorse
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride on this two-run maiden who has only raced twice, winning at 6f at Sandown on Standard; the step to 1m on Good to Firm is a significant unknown, and competing for the lead against Rocket Boy and Dandyman Dan could expose limitations in a stamina test.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, Firehorse arrives fit on a 19-day turnaround carrying 129 lb from stall 5; the fifth two starts back is the one question mark he must answer.

runners_data.name: My A'Ali Baba
runners_data.note: David Evans has this hold-up filly freshened on 13 days; her best form came at 6f on Soft, and both the step to 1m and the Good to Firm ground represent untested parameters — she is the lone genuine closer and needs the pace to truly collapse in front of her.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win four starts back but has been in and out of form since, going unplaced last time out; he has run over today's trip and going, arrives fit on 13 days' rest, but our rating of 92 suggests he's up against it from stall 4 off 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Quest For Stars
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's operation is firing (T14:10/27) and this unbeaten two-year-old (form 11 at 7f Good) is the standout form horse — Connor Planas partners a horse who has handled Good ground expertly and the mile trip looks well within range given two authoritative 7f wins.
runners_data.comment: Quest For Stars arrives in red-hot form, winning his last two starts, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; a trainer firing at 37% in the last fortnight adds further confidence, though carrying 129 lb from stall eight is the burden he must overcome.

runners_data.name: Rafe's Da Man
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon yard has solid numbers (T14:8/56) and Pat Dobbs partners a horse in good heart after a recent victory (form 4431, last win 7f Good); prominent style suits this race shape well and his four runs all on Good ground suggest reliable going preference.
runners_data.comment: Rafe's Da Man won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but his speed rating of 77 leaves him needing to find more, and he faces a stiff task ranked fifth of eight on our rating.

runners_data.name: Rocket Boy
runners_data.note: The standout on official ratings at OR=120, this Marco Botti-trained colt is unbeaten in one run (1/7f/GOO) and carries significant class into this field; Marco Ghiani pilots a horse who will want to lead and could simply be too good, though he must repel multiple rivals for the front end immediately.
runners_data.comment: Rocket Boy won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, so there are boxes ticked — but ranked seventh of eight on our figures, he faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals here.

runners_data.name: Velociraptor
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's runner has won at 7f on Good and placed at the same trip; David Probert rides a horse who naturally tracks pace from a prominent position, which is exactly the profile this race shape is likely to reward, and he handles the going with a 1W2P record on similar conditions.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and his speed rating of 72 gives little encouragement, though a win last time out and experience over today's trip and going at least offer something to work with from stall one.

runners_data.name: Scommessa Sicura
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over on Andrew Balding's filly (T14:8/57) who has been placed four times before finally winning at 7f Good most recently; she is a natural front-runner stepping into Listed company and her freshness on 34 days since last run is worth noting, though she will need to assert quickly against multiple rivals for the lead.
runners_data.comment: Scommessa Sicura arrives in fine fettle, winning last time out and placing in her three prior starts, with experience over today's trip and going adding confidence; drawn in stall seven carrying 124 lb, she is the one to beat.

races.paceDynamic: Rocket Boy, Dandyman Dan, Firehorse, and Scommessa Sicura all carry natural front-running profiles, with Quest For Stars also capable of racing prominently, meaning this 1m Salisbury contest will be contested at a fierce pace from the outset on Good to Firm ground. Four genuine lead-seekers cannot all occupy the same piece of real estate, so there will be immediate competition for the front, likely producing a searching gallop that stretches the field early and turns this into a true stamina examination over the mile trip. Rafe's Da Man and Velociraptor will track proceedings from a prominent position, while My A'Ali Baba is the lone confirmed hold-up runner and will likely find herself racing further off the pace than ideal given the tempo. The race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield stalkers with proven stamina — horses who can sit just off the speed, avoid the early battle for supremacy, and produce a sustained late run when the pace-setters inevitably come back to the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the battle between Rocket Boy, Dandyman Dan, Firehorse and Scommessa Sicura for the lead produces an unsustainable gallop and the front-runners tie each other up.
scenarios.body: The pace-setters burn each other out through a fast early sectional, leaving the race wide open entering the final two furlongs as the leaders capitulate; prominent types who travelled smoothly just off the pace are perfectly positioned to sprint clear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pace-Setter Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Rocket Boy, the highest-rated runner on OR=120, asserts dominance early and deters rivals into settling, creating a steadier but still-contested lead.
scenarios.body: Rocket Boy dictates on his own terms with rivals forced to track him at a comfortable clip, allowing a well-rated front-runner to control tempo and kick again from the front; this favours the horse with the highest class who can dictate and repel challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce that even the prominent trackers are compromised, and My A'Ali Baba is delivered with a powerful late sweep.
scenarios.body: My A'Ali Baba, the lone confirmed hold-up runner, would need absolute carnage up front and a clear, unobstructed run to make up significant ground on a flat track; the slim profile here reflects that this scenario requires multiple conditions to align simultaneously.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace, Front-Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the early lead battle dissipates quickly with one runner establishing dominance unchallenged and rivals accepting their fate at a sustainable tempo.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner in control at a manageable gallop retains enough in the tank to repel all challengers, with stamina questions for rivals who did not get the searching pace they needed; this is the least likely outcome given the volume of genuine pace-seekers entered.

watchPoints.text: Rocket Boy (OR=120) is significantly higher-rated than any rival — if Marco Ghiani secures the lead uncontested even briefly, he may prove impossible to reel in and the market could be underestimating his class advantage.

The early duel between Rocket Boy, Dandyman Dan, Firehorse, and Scommessa Sicura for front position is the defining tactical moment — whichever horse emerges in front with least pressure will hold a major advantage, and whichever burns most energy fighting for it faces near-certain defeat.

Quest For Stars is unbeaten for Appleby (2 from 2 at 7f Good) and Connor Planas may elect to sit prominently rather than lead, potentially tracking the chaos and unleashing a strong finish — her unbeaten record demands respect at any price.

My A'Ali Baba is the only true hold-up runner but her best form came on Soft going over shorter — on Good to Firm over 1m, Callum Shepherd will need everything to fall perfectly and the scenario is narrow.

The confirmed Good to Firm ground (despite the race card listing Good) is a meaningful detail — all runners are rated OK for the going, but horses with the most positive form on fast ground, particularly Rafe's Da Man and Quest For Stars, may hold a hidden edge.

races.name: Molson Coors Pembroke Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Bold Shout
runners_data.note: Clive Cox sends out a lightly raced three-year-old who has twice finished fourth, both times green and with improvement in the locker; Hector Crouch can track the leader from a prominent position and his 64-day break suggests a freshness angle, though sim-going form is thin at two runs.|

runners_data.name: It's A Mugs Game
runners_data.note: Sean Levey partners a hold-up horse whose recent form shows a distant fourth and a wide-margin win early in the sequence; returning quickly on 12 days' rest, its natural style places it at the back of a field that won't be generating the deep pace it needs to pounce.|

runners_data.name: Kodicall
runners_data.note: Taylor Fisher rides a horse that finished second on firm going and fifth on good, giving some encouragement on this surface; the hold-up profile is a disadvantage in a race compressed by multiple closers, though its 5f-to-6f progression is mildly interesting.|

runners_data.name: Annie Sioux
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand is booked by Clive Cox for an entirely unexposed debutante — no form string, no going data, no days since last run recorded — making this a true unknown that could range from uncompetitive to a serious threat; Marquand's ability to place a green horse in a stalking position off a single front-runner is the key variable.|

runners_data.name: Gris De Chine
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will control the race from the front, though the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.90 highlights that her field-level ability (OR 59) is markedly below rivals; Callum Shepherd has the tactical advantage of owning the lead but the class gap to horses rated 120 is significant.|

runners_data.name: Just Dreaming
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's seven-runner entrant has an OR of 41 and a modest form string of 5-75; a true hold-up horse whose position has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is over-subscribed — the horse's natural style will not be served here and its low rating compounds the problem.|

runners_data.name: Remi Mae
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a powerful booking for Andrew Balding's filly, who holds genuine 6f form on good ground including a second and a third; her hold-up style is her natural register but she is mapped to midfield due to the density of closers — Murphy's ability to manufacture a run from a less-than-ideal position is the angle to watch here.|

races.paceDynamic: Gris De Chine is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner novice and, with no rival able or willing to seriously challenge for the lead, will dictate an honest but uncontested gallop across Salisbury's flat six furlongs. The going report confirms Good to Firm conditions for this slot, favouring a true-run, relatively quick surface that rewards natural pace and clean air. Remi Mae and Just Dreaming are genuine hold-up horses by style, but with multiple closers in a small field they are unlikely to find the gaps and late momentum this race shape would ordinarily demand. This structure — one leader, a cluster of midfield or prominent types unable to get a clean position, and hold-up horses mapped forward under compression — strongly favours horses who can race just off the pace and pounce from a tracking position rather than those coming from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gris De Chine Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Gris De Chine bowls clear unchallenged and sets a true but sustainable gallop, the race is run on front-runner's terms.
scenarios.body: Gris De Chine, racing from her natural prominent position, sets a smooth tempo and the compressed hold-up brigade struggle to reel her in across six flat furlongs on quick ground; a prompt, economical gallop with daylight to the field is hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trio Fill Pocket
scenarios.trigger: If Bold Shout or Annie Sioux tracks Gris De Chine tightly and quickens off the bend with first run.
scenarios.body: A closer tracking the leader maintains momentum through the final two furlongs and angles clear before the hold-up horses can wind up; Good to Firm ground amplifies the advantage of a horse that doesn't lose ground in transit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and a clear gap materialises in the final furlong for a closer to exploit.
scenarios.body: Remi Mae's form at six furlongs on good ground makes her the most credible beneficiary if a genuine sprint develops, but she and Just Dreaming are both mapped forward of their natural position and must overcome that disadvantage; the scenario is contingent on conditions that this race shape does not strongly favour.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Tactical Race
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses jostle for position early, disrupting Gris De Chine's rhythm and compressing the field into a bunched sprint.
scenarios.body: A scrappy, uneven gallop suits an unexposed type capable of finding a length in a fast-finishing dash, but with such a small field a genuine melee is unlikely; Annie Sioux's complete absence of form data makes her a wildcard if connections have been quietly preparing her for this.

watchPoints.text: Gris De Chine's uncontested lead is real — watch whether Callum Shepherd is given any early company at all, as a wholly unchallenged fractions scenario is entirely plausible in this field.
Annie Sioux is a Clive Cox debutante with zero public form data; a well-prepared first-time starter with Tom Marquand aboard must be respected if early money appears in the market.

Remi Mae's redistribution from hold-up to midfield is forced by the field composition — watch Oisin Murphy's positioning in the early strides to see whether the filly gets any closer to the pace than her natural style suggests.
Bold Shout's 64-day absence is notable in a novice field; Clive Cox horses returning after a break often show improvement, and a run at Salisbury specifically may have been targeted here.

The field's OR ceiling of 120 for five runners versus 59 and 41 for Gris De Chine and Just Dreaming underscores a significant class split — the race shape may be dictated by the lowest-rated horse while the highest-rated ones resolve the outcome behind her.

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Upavon Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Alla Stella
runners_data.note: Consistent Listed-class hold-up performer for Prescott with five placed efforts, though her record in similar going (0W4P from six runs) flags a tendency to finish second or third rather than win; the step back up to 12f after several 10f runs suits her stamina profile and she has good form at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Alla Stella has finished second in each of her last two starts and brings strong recent consistency to this contest; drawn three and carrying 130 lb, the weight burden is the one factor to watch, though her experience over today's trip keeps her firmly in the mix.

runners_data.name: Goldilocks Cen
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes over for Archie Watson, but her recent form — a run of 9th, 5th, 14th — at shorter trips on similar or softer ground raises serious doubts about her current form; her natural preference is to race from further back than this race map suggests, but with rivals who also want to track, she may end up further off the pace than ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a win four starts back and filled the runner-up spot five starts back, but has disappointed in her last three outings since; she has run over today's going before and draws stall two carrying 130 lb, though recent form gives as much reason for caution as hope.

runners_data.name: Regal Charm
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's mare carries strong claims on form — a course winner and placed twice at this trip — and Rob Hornby's booking lends confidence; her prominent style fits the race shape cleanly with no redistribution concern, and three placed runs from seven outings on good ground show she handles this surface.|
runners_data.comment: Regal Charm shaped well with a second last time out following a win two starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and going. Carrying 130 lb from stall one, her rating of 106 marks her as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Annastarzy
runners_data.note: Three wins from her last four starts for Richard Hannon suggest a filly in terrific heart, but all that form was at 7-8f and she is stepping up sharply in trip and class here; her natural style pushes her forward but the race map shows she may struggle to secure a prominent berth, meaning she will likely race in a position that doesn't suit her best form.|
runners_data.comment: Three wins in her last six starts show Annastarzy has ability, but that sixth last time out is a concern, and ranked sixth of seven on our figures she faces a stiff ask here; the going holds no fears, at least.

runners_data.name: Felicitas
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's lightly-raced three-year-old is the race's lone front-runner and has earned an OR=103 from winning at 8f and placing twice at 10f — the step to 12f is unproven but she has a high cruising speed; 59 days off the track is the one flag, and though her style makes her the race-shaper, she carries a STYLE_FIT tag suggesting her lead role may not be as comfortable as it looks on paper.|
runners_data.comment: Felicitas landed back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and her second two starts back shows she retains ability — but that seventh last time out after 59 days off raises a fitness query she must answer here.

runners_data.name: Miss Scott
runners_data.note: The John & Thady Gosden-trained filly arrives with a polished two-from-three record including a win over 10f on good ground and has Oisin Murphy, her most high-profile booking; lightly raced at three, her prominent tracking style fits the likely race shape ideally and she looks the most natural beneficiary if Felicitas is run off her feet late.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of seven on our figures and her speed rating of 77 gives little encouragement, though Miss Scott arrives in fair nick — a winner last time out and again three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: On Message
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly won at 8f and placed at 10f on good ground but her last two runs — including a 7th over 12f on soft — raise minor trip and ground queries; Hector Crouch is a capable booking and her hold-up style gives her a chance if the pace is genuine, though she has yet to prove she truly stays 12f.|

races.paceDynamic: Felicitas is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with just one genuine pace-setter in a seven-runner field, she should be able to dictate terms unchallenged through the early stages of this 1m2f contest on good-to-firm ground at Salisbury. Regal Charm and Miss Scott are the natural prominent trackers who will sit just off Felicitas, giving the race a controlled, single-file shape rather than a contested burn-up. That sustainable gallop through the first half mile sets up a thorough stamina test over the final three furlongs, where the ability to quicken off a genuine but unhurried pace becomes the decisive factor. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with the acceleration to pick up from behind a steady-run pace — Alla Stella and On Message are best-placed stylistically, though both carry redistribution-adjacent caveats about this track and trip. The field holds more prominent-travelling types than the race can accommodate cleanly: Annastarzy and Goldilocks Cen, both genuine prominent or hold-up runners in their own right, are most likely to find themselves shuffled back rather than securing the position their form suggests they prefer.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Felicitas Dictates, Stays Honest
scenarios.trigger: If Felicitas controls pace throughout at a fair but sustainable clip, allowing her proven stamina to be the weapon.
scenarios.body: Felicitas leads on her own terms, setting a rhythm that doesn't burn off the prominent horses but keeps enough pressure on to stop closers looming too late; her OR=103 and winning form over 10f on good ground make her the class act if the race is run to suit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop Home
scenarios.trigger: If Felicitas's tempo is genuinely modest and the field concertinas in the final two furlongs, rewarding horses with a sharp late gear.
scenarios.body: A slowly-run first half sees the hold-up horses travel sweetly before unleashing their finishes in the final quarter-mile; Alla Stella with Sir Mark Prescott's patient handling and On Message's impressive Goodwood win both become live dangers in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuine enough to stretch the field but a prominent tracker rather than the leader lands the spoils.
scenarios.body: Regal Charm, who has placed at this trip on good and soft ground repeatedly, or Miss Scott, unbeaten in two runs over longer trips, press Felicitas from the outset and use the solid gallop to grind out a win as the leader ties up late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Open Finish, Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Felicitas sets a crawl that creates a sprint finish with the whole field arriving in a heap.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race bunches the field and produces a chaotic final furlong where positional luck and raw speed over a short burst matter most; Annastarzy's raw sprint figures and recent winning form at shorter trips make her the most dangerous if the race degenerates into a dash.

watchPoints.text: Felicitas (59 days off) — monitor her early energy and whether Kieran Shoemark elects to bowl along or ration the gallop; if she labours past halfway, Miss Scott and Regal Charm are primed to swoop.|

Annastarzy's draw and starting tactics could determine her entire race — if Hannon's team has briefed Joe Leavy to push forward early, she will burn energy fighting for position that likely cannot be maintained over 12f against classier fillies.|

Alla Stella's record of 0 wins from 4 placed efforts in similar going is a recurring pattern under Prescott — she often finds one too good; note whether she travels sweetly into the straight, as that is her critical passage.|

Goldilocks Cen's last three finishes (9th, 5th, 14th) at trips shorter than today's 12f suggest she needs the extra distance to fire — watch whether she finds a cleaner run than her recent races have allowed before drawing conclusions about form.|

Going report confirms Good to Firm across the card at Salisbury — the ground is consistent and drying, so any runner with a concern-flag on fast ground should be watched in the pre-race canter for any sign of discomfort.|

races.name: Champagne Joseph Perrier Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Londoner
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 86 and a confirmed front-runner; wears headgear and Marquand will use the prominent position, but the presence of Eupator means he cannot simply steal matters — his sim-going record of 0W1P from five starts on similar ground is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Londoner ran a cracker second last time out and returns on a quick 11-day turnaround fit and ready, with experience of both today's trip and going working in his favour; the concern is he's been beaten in his last five starts, so he must convert promise into victory.

runners_data.name: Fox Avatar
runners_data.note: Roger Varian runner returning from 44 days off with Oisin Murphy, a high-profile booking; has winning form at 12f on Tapeta suggesting stamina is there, but his similar-going record at just 1W2P from three starts on turf equivalent ground warrants monitoring for course fitness.
runners_data.comment: Fox Avatar showed a good turn of foot when winning three starts back, but has disappointed in his last two outings since; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 133 lb from stall 5, and the 44-day break leaves his current fitness open to question.

runners_data.name: Miss Tonnerre
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare for Ed Walker and Kieran Shoemark, absent 77 days so fitness is the headline question; her headgear notation suggests she has form quirks to manage, but if she arrives cherry-ripe this trip on Good to Firm suits and she is the natural style-beneficiary of a contested pace.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but Miss Tonnerre's ratings profile edges this field, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions. A fourth two starts back offers a flicker of encouragement; fourth from stall three, this is her spot to finally deliver.

runners_data.name: Almekarem
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's runner has form that reads well — a win 11 days ago at 10f on Good going — and Luke Morris will likely sit patiently off the pace in his natural hold-up role; Prescott's relatively quiet 14-day strike rate of 4/23 is the only minor caution.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well last time out after winning two starts back, Almekarem rates below the mark on our figures as only the sixth of seven on our ratings, though he has experience over today's trip and going, returns fit on 11 days' rest, and stall one is his lot.

runners_data.name: Eupator
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner under Sean Levey for Richard Hannon; his sim-going record of 0W2P from three starts suggests he rarely wins on this surface, and the head-to-head early battle with Londoner risks leaving him with nothing in the tank from two furlongs out.
runners_data.comment: Eupator has run over today's trip and going before, and his third last time out — alongside a second four starts back — shows he can get competitive; our rating of 83 suggests he holds strong claims, though he remains winless in recent starts and must bounce back from that sixth two runs ago.

runners_data.name: Carnival Day
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Jim Boyle with a strong placed record at this trip and going — 1W4P from eight similar-going starts — making him consistent if not a regular winner; Cosgrave will likely park him just off the lead pair and hope they tire.

runners_data.name: Mythical Bird
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's runner has the worst trainer 14-day figures in the field (0/4) and has placed form at 10f on Good ground; races prominently, so will try to tuck in behind the front-runners, but needs a significant improvement on recent efforts to feature.
runners_data.comment: Two unplaced efforts sandwiched around a third last time out make her hard to fancy ranked last on our figures, though she has distance and going experience and that sole win in her last five starts shows she can find the line.

races.paceDynamic: Londoner and Eupator are both confirmed front-runners in a field of just seven, meaning the lead will be contested from the outset over Salisbury's 1m2f on Good to Firm ground. Tom Marquand on Londoner and Sean Levey on Eupator will both have instructions to be prominent, and neither rider is likely to concede the initiative willingly, creating a genuinely contested gallop rather than a dawdle. Fox Avatar and Carnival Day will push up into prominent positions behind the lead pair, adding further pressure to the early and middle portions of the race. This race shape — with two genuine front-runners burning fuel and prominent horses close behind — classically favours hold-up or midfield horses that can track the pace without expending energy early, then pounce when the leaders tie up in the final two furlongs; Miss Tonnerre and Almekarem are the natural beneficiaries of this dynamic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Londoner and Eupator press each other through a genuine gallop and weaken in the final two furlongs, allowing the hold-up horses to run through them.
scenarios.body: The contested early pace drains both front-runners before the home straight, leaving Miss Tonnerre and Almekarem with reserves to pick up the pieces on the Good to Firm surface they both handle. Almekarem's recent win at 10f on Good going and Miss Tonnerre's hold-up profile place them perfectly in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lead pair — most likely Londoner — is allowed to control tempo without being severely pressured and gets first run.
scenarios.body: Londoner's experience at this trip and his prominent headgear suggest he can dictate if Eupator fails to engage hard early, potentially stealing enough of a break to hold on. At OR 86 he is the highest-rated front-runner in the field and Marquand is adept at judging pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steadier than expected and the prominent horses Fox Avatar and Carnival Day track a controlled gallop to pounce at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Oisin Murphy on Fox Avatar, returning from 44 days off for Roger Varian, is capable of travelling strongly just off the pace and delivering a sustained late challenge if the race does not become a burn-up. Carnival Day's consistent placed record at this trip and going band adds further weight to this shape if the fractions are modest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners clash badly, the field bunches, and a midfield runner benefits from a fortuitous split run.
scenarios.body: Mythical Bird has placed form at 10f on Good going and sits in the right position to benefit from any melee, though his trainer's recent form is very cold. This scenario requires genuine misfortune for the fancied runners and is a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Almekarem is the horse to watch as the race shape is tailored for his hold-up style and he arrives on the back of a win 11 days ago at the same trip on Good ground — if the front-runners burn each other off he is perfectly placed.

Londoner and Eupator will contest the lead from the outset; watch how hard each jockey pushes in the first half-mile, because if either cracks before the home straight it dramatically reduces that horse's chance of lasting.

Fox Avatar is returning from 44 days off for Varian with Murphy aboard — if he is forward enough in his work to handle the layoff he could be underestimated, but fitness on the day is impossible to confirm in advance.

Miss Tonnerre has been off 77 days and hold-up horses need to produce a finishing run — watch whether she gets a clear passage through the field in the home straight or gets hampered in the small field's drift.

The going report consistently lists the 5:00 race as Good to Firm, which is notably quicker than the headline Good — stamina reserves will be tested and horses with soft-ground recent form (Miss Tonnerre, Eupator) may find conditions less forgiving than their optimal.
